agency.name: Idaho Department of Fish and Game

overview: Idaho controlled hunt tags for deer, elk, pronghorn, moose, bighorn sheep, mountain goat, black bear and turkey are issued by random drawing; IDFG uses no preference or bonus points. In 2026, deer, elk, pronghorn and fall bear applications were taken May 1 - June 5 with a second drawing for unclaimed tags in August, and moose, sheep and goat applications April 1-30 (2027 dates not yet published). Nonresidents get no more than 10% of controlled hunt tags. Since 2026, nonresident general season deer and elk tags are also issued through a drawing held each December (2027 tags: December 5-15, 2026).

species.drawSystemSummary: Controlled hunt tags are issued by a random drawing; Idaho's drawing does not use preference or bonus points. Applicants may list a first and second hunt choice; second choices are drawn only from tags left after first choices. Anyone drawn in the first application period for a limited antlered-only elk hunt may not apply for another limited antlered-only elk hunt in the first application period of the following year.
species.residentNote: Residents buy general (zone) elk tags over the counter; capped elk zone tags have a first-come, first-served quota (2026 capped tags went on sale July 8; Sawtooth July 10). Residents who apply for a controlled elk hunt must wait five days after capped tags go on sale before buying one.
species.nonresidentNote: Since the 2026 season, nonresident general season deer and elk tags are issued through the Nonresident Tag Drawing (up to five hunt choices per application, groups of up to 4, $18.00 application fee). Statewide nonresident general-season quotas for 2027: 15,500 deer and 12,815 elk (including capped elk zones). In controlled hunts nonresidents get no more than 10% of tags (no more than one tag in hunts with 19 or fewer tags).
species.otcSummary: Resident general elk zone tags (capped zones limited, first-come first-served); leftover controlled tags after the second drawing.

species.drawSystemSummary: Moose tags are controlled hunts allocated by random drawing. A person may apply for only one of moose, bighorn sheep or mountain goat per year and is then barred from other big game controlled hunts that year (with listed exceptions). Anyone drawn must wait two years to apply again, and no one may take more than one antlered and one antlerless moose in Idaho in a lifetime (Super Hunt winners and leftover tag holders excepted).
species.residentNote: 2026 resident tag plus application: $183.50 (Price Lock) or $216.50 (no Price Lock), including the $16.75 application fee.
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents are limited to 10% of controlled hunt tags per species and no more than one tag in hunts with 10 or fewer tags; 2026 nonresident tag plus application $2,672.50.
species.otcSummary: None; leftover tags from the second drawing go on sale July 10.

coverage.notes: First drawing, first-choice counts per IDFG drawing-odds table; second-choice and second-drawing results in row notes. 2026 brochure total 18,670 controlled elk tags plus unlimited vs 18,515 in drawn hunts here; the difference is outfitter-allocated controlled hunts (e.g. 2175-2213) that are not publicly drawn and are absent from the odds table. 2023 hunt 2250 and 2024 hunt 2285 are listed twice by IDFG with different figures, so their counts are given only in the note. 2022-2024 outfitter-allocated hunts that IDFG lists with tags but zero applicants are omitted (not a public draw). Seven 2023 January Extra hunts (2250-2256) and 2025 hunt 2133 have no season dates because the Hunt Planner list did not identify a single matching tag.

Includes IDFG deer hunts listed for 'Mule Deer' or 'Mule and White-tailed Deer'; hunts with no matching hunt-list entry are kept here with a note. 2026 brochure total 13,226 controlled deer tags plus unlimited vs 12,923 in drawn deer hunts here (mule-deer + whitetail); the difference is outfitter-allocated hunts (e.g. 1148-1187) not in the odds table. 2022-2024 outfitter-allocated hunts listed with zero applicants are omitted.
Only IDFG controlled hunts listed for 'White-tailed Deer'.
2026 sum of limited-hunt tags (2,040) matches the brochure total '2,040 Tags Plus Unlimited Tags'. Unlimited hunts have quota null.

2025 antlered moose tags sum to 510, matching the brochure '510 Tags'. 2026 hunt metadata (season dates, antler class) come from the 2025 & 2026 brochure because the Hunt Planner list has no 2026 moose/sheep/goat hunts (hunt 3050, whose odds-table area label differs, is matched by hunt number, tags and an unchanged area description in seasons_ranges.py). IDFG published no second-drawing odds for moose, sheep or goat.

Rocky Mountain (5xxx) and California (7xxx) bighorn hunts combined. 2026 dates from the 2025 & 2026 brochure; two 2026 rows (5027, 5028) have none because the odds table's hunt area ('Bannock', '37') differs from the brochure's (37L, 37AL).

2026 season dates from the 2025 & 2026 brochure where hunt area and tags match; hunts 6018 and 6019 matched by hunt number, tags and an unchanged area description (odds table relabeled 51 -> 51-1, 61 -> 61-1).

sources.title: IDAPA 13.01.04 – Rules Governing Licensing (Idaho Administrative Code)
sources.publisher: Idaho Department of Fish and Game
sources.notes: Current rule text (sections 330 and 801 carry effective date 7-1-26). Section 801.05.b fixes the Super Hunt (Special Controlled Hunt Program) application deadlines every year: May 31 for the June drawing and August 10 for the August drawing. Section 330.01 leaves all other controlled hunt application periods, tag claim deadlines and leftover sales to dates the Department publishes.
